name: Charalambides
label: Kranky
lede: Two Houston record-store clerks named their band after a customer, married, divorced, kept playing, and survived a Berlin intensive-care ward to make their thirtieth-odd album.

eras.title: A record store, a roommate and a customer's surname
eras.text: Tom Carter and Christina Carter met working at Sound Exchange, a Houston record store. With Tom's college roommate Kyle Silfer they started playing in late 1991, first as Mutual Admiration Society.

years.src: The Self-Portrait Gospel: Tom Carter interview · COTFG: Christina Carter interview · Wikipedia
years.h: Tom Carter, Christina Carter and Kyle Silfer start a band in Houston
years.p: Tom and Christina Carter met at Houston's Sound Exchange record store. Kyle Silfer, Tom's college roommate, made it a trio in late 1991.
years.xp:
Tom Carter grew up in Maryland and Ohio and came to Houston on a scholarship to the University of Houston, where he took an English degree. From 1989 to 1993 he also played in the Houston band The Mike Gunn.

Carter remembers Silfer playing guitar overhand, picking with his thumb. The group first called itself Mutual Admiration Society; Christina Carter dates the real start of Charalambides to 1991.

years.src: Wikipedia
years.h: Charalambides: the band is named after a record store customer
years.p: Charalambides takes its name from the surname of a customer at the Houston record shop where Tom and Christina Carter met.

eras.title: Siltbreeze says yes to everything
eras.text: Tom Lax's Philadelphia label Siltbreeze, home of Harry Pussy and other outsider noise, gave Charalambides vinyl and room to sprawl. Christina Carter says Siltbreeze let them think in double albums from the start, without interference.

years.src: Wikipedia · The Self-Portrait Gospel
years.h: Our Bed Is Green · a self-released 100-minute cassette
years.p: After Kyle Silfer leaves, Tom and Christina Carter put out a C-100 tape themselves as a duo. Kranky reissues Our Bed Is Green as a double CD in 2005.
years.xp: A second self-released tape, Historic 6th Ward, followed in 1994. The band's own Wholly Other label put it on CD in 1996, and Time-Lag pressed it as a double LP in 2002.

years.src: The Self-Portrait Gospel: Tom Carter interview
years.h: Jason Bill joins Charalambides for a Siltbreeze festival in Philadelphia
years.p: Siltbreeze founder Tom Lax books Charalambides for his festival at the Khyber in Philadelphia. Tom and Christina Carter add guitarist Jason Bill to fill out the sound.

years.src: Wikipedia: Siltbreeze · The Other Side of Life
years.h: Union: the first Charalambides LP, on Siltbreeze
years.p: Tom Lax's Siltbreeze gives Charalambides its first vinyl, a label Lax had founded in 1989 out of his own fanzine.

years.src: Wikipedia · COTFG: Christina Carter interview
years.h: Market Square · the first Charalambides double LP
years.p: The second Siltbreeze record, and the first double album. The same year Playtime issues a 7-inch, Devils backed with Bid You Goodnight.

years.src: The Self-Portrait Gospel: Tom Carter interview · Wikipedia
years.h: The Charalambides trio falls apart after disastrous shows
years.p: Tom Carter says the three-piece with Jason Bill ended around 1996 after a run of bad shows. Bill moved to El Paso and the Carters went back to being a duo.
years.xp: The trio years included touring with Siltbreeze labelmates Harry Pussy. By then the band had its own label, Wholly Other, releasing records since 1995.

eras.title: Wholly Other, and a pedal steel
eras.text: Charalambides ran on its own label now, much of it hand-numbered CD-Rs in editions of 100 to 250. Houston-raised Heather Leigh Murray brought pedal steel and a third voice, and the band landed in the circle of Six Organs of Admittance later filed as New Weird America.

years.src: Wikipedia
years.h: Houston · a Charalambides album named for home
years.p: The band's last album on Tom Lax's Siltbreeze before the move to Kranky.

years.src: The Self-Portrait Gospel · Tiny Mix Tapes · Noisey
yt: Live at Texas Psych Fest 2002, with Heather Leigh
years.h: Heather Leigh Murray joins Charalambides on pedal steel
years.p: West Virginia-born, Houston-raised Heather Leigh Murray becomes the third member around 2000. She stays through Joy Shapes.
years.xp: Murray also formed Scorces with Christina Carter, a duo of pedal steel and voices, and played in Houston's Taurpis Tula. She later worked with Jandek and Peter Brötzmann under the name Heather Leigh.

years.src: Tom Carter on Bandcamp: YIH · Wikipedia
years.h: YIH, 100 copies, and a split LP with Six Organs of Admittance
years.p: Carbon Records issues the Austin-recorded duo improvisation YIH in 100 copies. Timelag pairs Charalambides with Ben Chasny's Six Organs of Admittance on a split LP.
years.xp: On YIH Tom Carter plays lap steel, bells and music box and Christina Carter plays chord organ and sings; the cover art is by Joe Tunis. The double LP IN CR EA SE followed on Eclipse in 2002.

eras.title: Kranky, and a marriage that ended mid-album
eras.text: Kranky gave Charalambides real distribution for the first time. The best-known run of records came while the Carters' marriage came apart, Tom moved to California and Heather Leigh Murray moved to Scotland.

years.src: Wikipedia · Tiny Mix Tapes
years.h: Unknown Spin · a CD-R split, rescued by Kranky
years.p: The first Charalambides album on Kranky is the band's half of a 2002 Wholly Other CD-R split with Scorces, Christina Carter's duo with Heather Leigh Murray.

years.src: The Other Side of Life (2005) · The Self-Portrait Gospel · Wikipedia
years.h: Joy Shapes · recorded entirely in the Carters' home
years.p: Tom Carter says all of Joy Shapes was recorded at home, edited from 4-track to DAT. Jerry Tubb mastered it at his Austin studio.
years.xp: It was Heather Leigh Murray's last record with the band. Extra material from the sessions came out as Electricity Ghost on Wholly Other in 2007.

years.src: The Self-Portrait Gospel: Tom Carter interview · The Other Side of Life · Wikipedia
years.h: Tom and Christina Carter divorce, and Charalambides carries on
years.p: Tom Carter says his and Christina Carter's protracted breakup and divorce played out during Joy Shapes. In early 2004 he took a bookstore job in Berkeley.
years.xp: Tom settled in Oakland while Christina stayed in Texas; by 2005 the two lived far apart and made records anyway. Wikipedia still describes them as divorced but a musical unit.

q: Heather fell in love and moved to Glasgow.
years.src: The Other Side of Life (2005) · Tiny Mix Tapes
years.h: Heather Leigh Murray leaves Charalambides for Glasgow
years.p: Murray moves to Glasgow, where she co-runs the Volcanic Tongue shop and label with writer David Keenan. Charalambides is a duo again.

years.src: The Self-Portrait Gospel · Wikipedia
years.h: A Vintage Burden · Tom and Christina Carter with Andrew MacGregor
years.p: The third Kranky album of new music, made by the Carters with Andrew MacGregor while Tom lived in Oakland.

years.src: Wikipedia
years.h: Likeness · the fourth Charalambides album on Kranky
years.p: A Kranky CD. The same year Wholly Other releases Strangle the Wretched Heavens, recorded 1994–96.

eras.title: Berlin
eras.text: Exile was the last Charalambides album on Kranky. On the European tour that followed, Tom Carter nearly died in a Berlin hospital, and a network of fellow musicians paid his bills.

years.src: Wikipedia · Houston Chronicle
years.h: Exile · the last Charalambides album on Kranky
years.p: The fifth Kranky album of new music. The Houston Chronicle later noted Christina Carter's lyrics and voice pushed further to the fore.

q: Forty days in intensive care and three weeks in another facility
years.src: Houston Press · INDY Week · Houston Chronicle
years.h: Tom Carter falls into a coma in a Berlin hospital
years.p: On a European tour, Tom Carter checks into a Berlin hospital with pneumonia and goes into septic shock. Doctors put him in a medically induced coma.
years.xp:
Carter says he checked in hoping for antibiotics before the tour moved on to Glasgow, then blacked out. He spent about 40 days in intensive care, then moved in mid-July to a rehabilitation clinic in Ahrenshoop on the Baltic coast. The Houston Chronicle later reported it left him with a lasting heart-rhythm problem.

Treated out of network and overseas, he faced bills his insurance might not cover, and ex-wife and bandmate Christina Carter spoke for the band in the press.

years.src: Exclaim! · INDY Week · Houston Press
years.h: Music for Tom Carter: a benefit album for his medical bills
years.p: A benefit compilation with Bill Orcutt, Pete Swanson, [[Jefre Cantu-Ledesma|9b69c184-919f-4db2-a2a4-995024f69334]] and others sends all proceeds to Tom Carter. Benefit shows ran from Houston and Chapel Hill to San Francisco and Portugal.
years.xp: Three Lobed Recordings gave Carter the proceeds from its unsold stock of his records, and donations went to a trust through helptomcarter.org. Exclaim reported he could not work or tour until the following year at the earliest.

eras.title: Home to Houston, under their own names
eras.text: After years apart in California, New York and elsewhere, both Carters were living in Houston again by 2018. Christina Carter says the album they cut in 2017 was the last time she recorded a note for years.

years.src: The Vinyl District · The Reveille (KLSU) · Houston Chronicle · COTFG
years.h: Charalambides: Tom and Christina Carter on Drawing Room
years.p: A double LP recorded in three days with engineers Ryan Edwards and Shannon Smith, with no plan going in. The Vinyl District counted more than 30 full-length Charalambides releases by then.
years.xp: Tom had moved back to Houston from New York around 2016, and Christina followed; the Houston Chronicle billed a show at Lawndale Art Center as their first Houston date in nearly a decade. The duo toured Europe that November.
